title: How to Use IB Psychology Past Papers in Final Weeks
summary: IB Psychology past papers can guide your final weeks: time attempts, mark carefully, log errors, and repair weak topics with a focused exam revision plan.
body_markdown:
The final weeks before an IB Psychology exam can feel deceptive. You recognize the studies and command terms, yet recognition is different from producing a precise answer under pressure.


Archived IB Psychology exam papers become useful when you follow a clear cycle: attempt, mark, diagnose, repair, and reattempt. Their value lies in revealing where marks disappear, whether through missing evidence, thin evaluation, misunderstood questions, or poor timing. Each attempt should change what you practise next.


### Your final-weeks practice checklist


- Confirm that questions match your syllabus and examination session.
- Complete a timed attempt without notes.
- Mark against the relevant criteria.
- Record knowledge gaps and technique errors separately.
- Repair the weakest area, then test it again.
- Combine targeted questions with complete simulations.


Syllabus alignment matters. The previous IB Psychology course had its final assessment in 2026; the revised course is first assessed in 2027. Students preparing for 2027 or later should use simulations aligned with the revised assessment model. Older questions may support selected skills without accurately reproducing the current paper structure.


### Begin with diagnosis


One carefully reviewed attempt can teach more than several papers completed without feedback. Start with a timed diagnostic: either a complete paper matching your course or a substantial section testing several skills. Work without notes, model answers, or timer extensions.


When time ends, annotate what happened before rewriting anything. Did you misunderstand a command term? Spend too long describing one study? Present evidence without connecting it to your argument?


The[guide to structuring IB answers](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/structure-ib-answers-maximum-marks) can help distinguish missing knowledge from weak answer construction. These require different remedies: revising another study will not necessarily improve an argument that never addresses the question.


### Make timed practice realistic


Timing means making decisions while the clock moves. Before starting, allocate time for reading, planning, writing, and checking according to your paper structure and teacher guidance. A brief plan helps keep your answer focused.


Use an uninterrupted timer, keep your phone away, and practise in the response format expected for your examination arrangements. Stop when time expires. An unfinished paragraph gives you information about pacing that an extra five minutes would conceal.


A student questions a clock about disappearing exam time


Alternate full simulations with focused sets. The[RevisionDojo Questionbank](https://www.revisiondojo.com/features/questionbank) supports targeted practice, while this[guide to using an IB question bank effectively](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/ib-question-bank-or-how-to-use-it-effectively) explains how to move from learning a topic to testing performance. Reserve enough time afterwards to review each attempt.


### Self-mark with the IB Psychology markscheme


Self-marking is difficult because you remember what you intended to say. Assess only what appears on the page.


Open the relevant markscheme and assessment criteria after finishing. Identify where your response demonstrates knowledge, application, evidence, analysis, and evaluation, as required by that question. Then highlight unsupported claims and paragraphs that drift from the prompt.


The[IB Psychology mark scheme guide](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/ib-psychology-mark-scheme-a-student-s-complete-guide) explains assessment expectations. Compare your reasoning with[IB Psychology Paper 1 sample answers](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/ib-psychology-paper-1-sample-answers-how-to-learn-from-them) only where the examples match your course version and assessed skills.


Translate feedback into an instruction you can use:


- **Weak evaluation:** Explain how a limitation affects the conclusion.
- **Limited relevance:** Connect each main paragraph to the specific question.
- **Thin evidence:** Explain how the study's findings support your claim.


RevisionDojo's Grading tools can provide additional feedback. Discuss uncertain judgments with your teacher, especially when you cannot explain why your response belongs in a particular mark band.


### Keep an error log that produces action


An error log needs four fields: question or topic, error type, likely cause, and next action. Write enough detail to guide another session. “Bad evaluation” offers little direction; “identified a limitation without explaining its effect” identifies a repair.


Separate knowledge, interpretation, structure, evidence, evaluation, and timing errors. Review the log after every few attempts and look for patterns rather than treating each mistake as isolated.


If terminology stays vague, revisit Study Notes and build a small Flashcards set. If choosing research takes too long, use AI Chat to practise recalling suitable evidence, checking explanations against course materials. For persistent reasoning problems, try narrower questions and seek feedback from your teacher or Tutors.


### Repair weak topics through retrieval


Rereading can create familiarity without showing whether you can retrieve an explanation independently. Close your notes and reconstruct the concept, supporting research, limitations, and links to a question.


A focused repair session follows three steps:


- Review the missing concept using concise notes.
- Retrieve it through flashcards or a blank-page summary.
- Apply it to a fresh question without support.


Return to the original question several days later. Build a new plan rather than memorizing a model response. Compare attempts for a specific improvement, such as clearer evidence or more relevant evaluation. The[guide to practising for real IB marks](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/making-the-most-of-ib-question-banks-and-practice-papers) develops this feedback-and-reattempt approach.


### Plan the final weeks around review


Begin with diagnosis and targeted repair, then add complete rehearsals as your understanding improves. During the final days, revisit recurring errors, maintain manageable practice, and protect sleep. Avoid scheduling a demanding paper when you cannot review it afterwards.


Use Predicted Papers and Mock Exams when they match your syllabus; treat them as practice rather than forecasts. RevisionDojo brings these together with its Questionbank, Study Notes, Flashcards, AI Chat, Grading tools, Coursework Library, and Tutors. This[overview of IB practice resources and AI study tools](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/effective-ib-practice-resources-ai-study-tools) helps match resources to the task.


The goal is fewer repeated mistakes. Use RevisionDojo to move from a timed attempt to a specific repair, then test that repair under pressure. That is how a collection of questions becomes a practical revision plan.
